name: Diamond (25°C multiple-reflection lattice measurement)
citation: T. Hom, W. Kiszenik and B. Post (1975). Accurate lattice constants from multiple reflection measurements. II. Lattice constants of germanium silicon, and diamond. Journal of Applied Crystallography 8, 457–458. DOI: 10.1107/S0021889875010965.
conditions_evidence: Original CIF explicitly states T=25°C and _diffrn_ambient_temperature 298.15 K. Numeric pressure is not supplied and remains unknown.
method: Experimental multiple X-ray diffraction measurements of a diamond platelet; original publisher abstract confirms a=3.566986 Å based on multiple reflections. Coordinates and space-group encoding are from the unmodified COD/AMCSD structure record.
synthesis_conditions_note: Original CIF reports compound source unknown; no growth/synthesis conditions asserted.
selection: Experimental diamond lattice measurement with explicit temperature; one symmetry-equivalent carbon site, complete tetrahedral C–C first shell.
notes: COD revision 306922 (2026-09-29) includes uncertainties from the original paper. Revision 306921 corrected an earlier mistyped c cell length using the original publication and AMCSD 0012842; the downloaded current cubic cell has a=b=c=3.566986 Å.

The carbon site multiplicity is 8 with population weight 1; four first neighbors are at 1.544550245 Å. This is a diamond sp3 environment and does not represent graphite, organics or all carbon K-edge spectra.
CIF spells the second author Kiszenick; the original publisher spells Kiszenik. Raw CIF bytes retain the database spelling, while the citation follows the publisher.

Low-energy light-element K-edge FEFF paths are unvalidated candidate scattering references, not a demonstration of usable measured EXAFS or XANES accuracy. Core excitons, band structure, charge transfer and nonspherical potentials can matter near these edges; retain actual SCF convergence, potential and executable diagnostics.

A nominal native k grid is not an experimental usable k range. Choose an absorber/edge-appropriate measured range and validate against data; a converged FEFF calculation alone does not validate this reference.
